channel.title: Wire — Security
channel.description: Security from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Keyv and friends compromised in active Shai-Hulud supply chain attack
item.description: Mini Shai-Hulud malware was injected into keyv and eight related npm packages on August 4, 2026 after an attacker compromised the maintainer's GitHub account (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: npm Staged Publishing Available, Adding a Human Approval Step before Packages Go Live
item.description: npm has introduced staged publishing for Node.js, requiring maintainer approval before a version is installable. Versions are queued and must pass a two-factor authentication challenge for release. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: GitHub Hardens npm and Actions Defaults, Drawing Debate over Delays versus Signing
item.description: GitHub consolidated the npm and Actions changes it shipped from March to July 2026 against supply chain attacks, several of which alter defaults rather than add options. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Buildpacks Move the Container Hardening Control Point Away From the Dockerfile
item.description: Cloud Native Buildpacks, which graduated within the CNCF in July 2026, move base image choice out of per-service Dockerfiles into a single builder owned by platform engineering, enabling fleet-wide patching. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Bringing Post-Quantum Cryptography to Java LTS Releases
Web Security is Too Hard
item.description: It started innocently enough. I saw a tweet about a new product offering from one of my favorite companies, Cloudflare. Neat! I clicked through to the site and there it is: And huzzah!, my preferred handle, @ericlaw is still available. (1 source: hackernews)
